chunks: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Isḥāq ibn Ghālib who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Isḥāq, how many do you think are the companions of this verse? {If they are given some of it they are pleased, but if they are not given from it they get enraged}, then he said to me: 'They are more than two-thirds of the people.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الْآيَةِ: Companions of the verse; those to whom a specific Quranic verse refers

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'companions of the verse' mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah 9:58 according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the 'companions of the verse' as those whose contentment is entirely contingent upon material gain, noting that such individuals constitute more than two-thirds of humanity. This hadith, found in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere poverty, but as freedom from the tyranny of worldly desire, a condition rare among the masses. The reference to 'more than two-thirds' serves as a poignant critique of societal norms, highlighting how the majority are enslaved by the very world they seek to possess.
